thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Higher, Dow Hits Record as Italy Budget Woes Ease; Street Mulls ADP Jobs, Services Data

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Higher, Dow Hits Record as Italy Budget Woes Ease; Street Mulls ADP Jobs, Services Data
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Wednesday's regular session:
iShares Inc iShares MSCI Brazil ETF ( EWZ ): +3.2%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +1.2%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.4%
VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ): -0.9%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ):-0.2%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was up 0.5%.
US stocks were higher at session's half after Italy's concession to lower its budget deficit target to 2.0% triggered a relief rally across Europe and the US. Led higher by a larger-than-expected increase in private payrolls and 13-year high in a leading measure of the services sector of the economy, the Dow Jones Industrial Average set another record high on outsized gains in Apple (AAPL) Boeing (BA) and Caterpillar (CAT).
The services sector came into focus Wednesday with both the ADP private payroll data, purchasing managers and Institute for Supply Management indices. Service-providing industries created 184,000 new jobs in September, surpassing a modest 46,000 gain in the goods-producing sector for a total of 230,000 new jobs in the private sector. This beat expectations for a 179,000 gain and followed an upwardly revised 168,000 increase in August.
The final September PMI for services was down slightly from August, but a revision to 53.5 from the preliminary 52.9 was still above Wall Street's expectations.
A comparable index from the ISM, however, rose to its highest level since 2005 of 61.6 from 58.5 in August, comfortably above the consensus estimate for a slight drop to 58.0.
Power Play: Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 1.2%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 2.5% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 2.5%.
FlexShopper (FPAY) rose more than 12% after the lease-to-own retailer reported Q3 gross lease originations jumped 90%. Gross lease originations rose to $12.4 million from $6.5 million in a the same period a year ago. For the nine months through Sept. 30, gross lease originations rose 47% to $30.8 million compared with $20.9 million in the same period last year.
Winners and Losers
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 0.6% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were in the green.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was up 0.6% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 0.6%.
Comcast (CMCSA) edged lower after it said that it has been selected by the State of Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology to deliver high-capacity fiber optic services to state agencies, including counties, cities and schools.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 1% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 1%.
Exxon Mobil (XOM) and Qatar Petroleum received European Commission approval for the acquisition of joint control of two Argentinian affiliates of Exxon. The commission approved the takeover of ExxonMobil Exploration Argentina and Mobil Argentina, according to a statement Wednesday. ExxonMobil Exploration Argentina has been active in the Vaca Muerta shale field in Argentina since 2010, according to Exxon's website, which it says "is considered one of the most important unconventional resources in the world." The commission decided that "the proposed transaction would raise no competition concerns because of the negligible actual and foreseen activities of the companies in the European Economic Area," the commission said in a statement. XOM shares fell marginally.
Commodities
Crude was up 1.3%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.4%. Natural gas was up 2.1% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 2.8%.
Gold was down 0.4%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.4%. Silver was up 0.1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.07%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was up 0.1% and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 0.8%.
Denali Therapeutics (DNLI) and biotechnology company Centogene said Wednesday that they have entered into a strategic collaboration for the global identification and recruitment of LRRK2 mutation carrier Parkinson's disease (PD) patients in clinical trials. Under the agreement, Centogene will conduct a targeted global recruitment campaign focused on the early identification and characterization of LRRK2 PD patients and sequencing of the LRRK2 gene in these patients using CentoCard, its proprietary, validated, dried blood spot collection kit. DNLI shares were down 2.5%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 0.3% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were lower.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was up 0.2% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were firmer.
Honda Motor (HMC) fell more than 3% after it said it is is set to invest a total of $2.75 billion in an initiative with General Motors (GM) to develop an autonomous vehicle for GM's Cruise that could be manufactured at high volumes. Cruise, GM and Honda "will explore global opportunities for commercial deployment of the Cruise network," the companies said in a statement on Wednesday. Honda will invest $2 billion over 12 years and put a $750 million equity investment into Cruise. That follows recent investments into Cruise from Japan's SoftBank Group and brings the "post-money valuation of Cruise to $14.6 billion," the companies said.
